title: Execution of the second layout stage
statement: Let $N$ be a finite nondeterministic Turing machine with Boolean input symbols, and let $y,x,w,w',r$ be Boolean words with $y$ equal to the nested pair encoding of $x$, the pair encoding of $w$, and the pair encoding of $w'$ with remainder $r$. Let $R$ be a register record and $s$ a natural number. Suppose every register of $R$ is at most $(8W(N)+8)(|y|+1)$, and that $R.B=2|x|+2|w|+4$, $R.P=2|x|+2|w|+2|w'|+6$, $R.S=s\le 2|y|$, $R.Wp$ is the length of the binary representation of $|x|$, and $R.E2=R.F2=R.T=R.Pos2=0$. Then either $|w'|=W(N)(2s+1)+R.Wp+1$ and the bit of $w'$ at position $W(N)(2s+1)+R.Wp$ is true, in which case the step-mode program reaches the input-checking stage from the copying stage with registers set as follows: $E2=b+4W(N)s+2W(N)$, $F2=b+4W(N)s+2W(N)+2R.Wp$, $U=b+4W(N)s+2W(N)+2R.Wp+4$, $Q1=b+4W(N)s+2W(N)$, $Pos2$ equal to the value of the first $R.Wp$ bits of $w'$ after its first $W(N)(2s+1)$ bits are dropped, and $T=0$, where $b=2|x|+2|w|+4$; or this length-and-bit condition fails, and the step-mode program halts with answer false. In both cases, the run satisfies the register bound and safety condition at every time before its endpoint.
hypotheses_covered: $N$ is a finite nondeterministic Turing machine over Boolean symbols
$y,x,w,w',r$ are Boolean words with the specified nested pair encoding
Every register of $R$ is bounded by $(8W(N)+8)(|y|+1)
